- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 10–30% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., +1.00), model often overshoots; apply a 20–40% downward correction to forecast 3–5 days ahead.  
- If model forecast is >3σ above recent mean, treat as overconfident; apply mean reversion heuristic: subtract 0.5–1.0x the deviation from forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model is prone to noise; use 30-day moving average as baseline for correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often fails to capture it; adjust downward by 15–25% for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment turns from negative to positive mid-period, model may lag; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 2–3 days ahead.
